title: Homily I — The grace of this feast and the duty to speak

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily I on the Dormition, col. 705 (PDF leaf 394)

source_text: Ὁρᾶτε, φίλοι Θεῷ Πατέρες καὶ ἀδελφοὶ, τῆς παρούσης ἡμέρας τὴν χάριν. Ὁρᾶτε, τῆς νῦν εὐφημουμένης τὸ ὑψηλὸν καὶ σεβάσμιον; Οὐ φρικώδη τὰ ταύτης μυστήρια; οὐ θαύματος γέμοντα; μακάριοι οἱ ὁρῶντες, ὡς ἰδεῖν πρεπωδέστατον. Μακάριοι οἱ νοερὰν κτησάμενοι αἴσθησιν! Οἷαι φωτὸς ἀστραπαὶ τὴν παροῦσαν νύκτα καταφαιδρύνουσιν! οἷαι ἀγγέλων δορυφορίαι τὴν τῆς ζωαρχικῆς μητρὸς καταγλαΐζουσι κοίμησιν· οἷαι ἀποστόλων θεηγορίαι τὴν κηδείαν τοῦ Θεοδόχου σώματος μακαρίζουσιν! Πῶς ὁ τοῦ Θεοῦ Λόγος, ὁ ταύτης υἱὸς δι' εὐσπλαγχνίαν γενέσθαι καταδεξάμενος, δεσποτικαῖς παλάμαις τῇ παναγίᾳ ταύτῃ καὶ θειοτάτῃ οἷα μητρὶ λειτουργῶν, τὴν ἱερὰν ψυχὴν ὑποδέχεται; Ὢ ἀγαθοῦ νομοθέτου! μὴ ὑποκείμενος νόμῳ, τὸν νόμον πληρῶν, ὃν αὐτὸς ἐνετείλατο. Αὐτὸς γὰρ τοῖς γονεῦσι τὴν ὀφειλὴν τοὺς παῖδας νέμειν ἐθεσμοθέτησε. Τίμα, φησὶ, τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα σου. Ὅτι δὲ ἀληθὲς τοῦτο, παντί που δῆλον, τῷ κἂν μικρὸν γοῦν τῶν θείων τῆς ἁγίας Γραφῆς μεταμεμυημένων λογίων. Εἰ γὰρ, ὥς φησιν ἡ θεία Γραφὴ, ψυχαὶ δικαίων ἐν χειρὶ Κυρίου, οὐχ αὐτὴ μᾶλλον ταῖς χερσὶ τοῦ Υἱοῦ καὶ Θεοῦ αὐτῆς τὴν ψυχὴν παρατίθεται. Ἀληθὴς ὁ λόγος, καὶ πάσης ἀντιλογίας ὑπέρτερος. Ἀλλ' εἰ δοκεῖ, τίς αὕτη, καὶ πόθεν, καὶ πῶς τῷ παρόντι χαρισθεῖσα βίῳ, δῶρον ἁπάντων τῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ δωρημάτων ὑψηλότερον ἅμα καὶ προσφιλέστερον δέδοται. Οἵαν τε τὴν ἐν τῷδε τῷ βίῳ διατριβὴν πεποίηται, καὶ οἵων μυστηρίων ἠξίωται, διεξίωμεν. Εἰ γὰρ τοὺς κατοιχομένους ἐπιταφίοις γεραίροντες Ἕλληνες, πᾶν ὅτιπερ ἑώρων ἀγώγιμον, πάσῃ σπουδῇ συνεισέφερον, ὡς ἂν τῷ μὲν εὐφημουμένῳ κατηρτισμένον τὸ ἐγκώμιον γένηται, τοῖς δὲ λειπομένοις, ζῆλος ἅμα πρὸς ἀρετὴν καὶ παράκλησις· μύθοις δὲ ὡς τὰ πολλὰ καὶ ἀπείροις πλάσμασι τὸν λόγον ἐξύφαινον, οἴκοθεν μὴ κεκτημένων τῶν ὑμνουμένων ἔπαινον· πῶς ἡμεῖς τὰ λίαν ἀληθῆ καὶ σεβάσμια, καὶ ὄντως ὄντα τοῖς πᾶσιν εὐλογίας ἁπάσης καὶ σωτηρίας πρόξενα, σιγῆς βυθοῖς τὸ τοῦ λόγου καλύψαντες, οὐ πολὺν ὀφλήσομεν γέλωτα, καὶ τῷ κατακρύψαντι τὸ τάλαντον τῆς αὐτῆς δίκης τευξόμεθα; τῆς συντομίας τοῦ λόγου φροντίζοντες, ὡς ἂν μὴ ταῖς ἀκοαῖς πολέμιος γένηται, ὡς τροφὴ τοῖς σώμασιν ὑπερβάλλουσα.
pass_a_gloss: See (ὁράω), friends to God (φίλοι Θεῷ) fathers and brothers, the grace (χάρις) of the present day. See the height (ὑψηλόν) and venerableness (σεβάσμιον) of the one now praised? Are not her mysteries (μυστήρια) awesome (φρικώδη)? Not full of wonder (θαῦμα)? Blessed (μακάριοι) those who see, as most fitting to see. Blessed those who have acquired noetic perception! What lightnings (ἀστραπαί) of light brighten the present night! What escorts (δορυφορίαι) of angels make splendid (καταγλαΐζω) the falling-asleep (κοίμησις) of the life-originating (ζωαρχικός) mother; what God-speakings (θεηγορίαι) of apostles bless the funeral (κηδεία) of the God-receiving (Θεοδόχος) body! How the Word of God, who through compassion accepted (καταδέχομαι) to become her son, with masterly palms serving (λειτουργέω) this all-holy and most divine one as a mother, receives (ὑποδέχομαι) the holy soul? O good lawgiver (νομοθέτης)! Not subject to law (νόμος), fulfilling (πληρόω) the law which he himself commanded. For he himself enacted (θεσμοθετέω) that children render (νέμω) the debt (ὀφειλή) to parents. Honour (τιμάω), he says, the father and your mother. That this is true is clear to everyone who has been initiated (μυέω) even a little in the divine oracles (λόγια) of holy Scripture. For if, as divine Scripture says, souls of the just in the hand of the Lord, does not she rather deposit (παρατίθεμαι) her soul in the hands of her Son and God? True the word, and above all contradiction (ἀντιλογία). But if it seems good, who she is, and whence, and how, graced (χαρίζομαι) to the present life, she has been given as a gift higher and dearer than all the gifts (δωρήματα) of God; and what sojourn (διατριβή) she made in this life, and of what mysteries she was deemed worthy (ἀξιόω), let us go through (διέξειμι). For if the Greeks (Ἕλληνες), honouring the departed with epitaphs (ἐπιτάφιοι), contributed with all zeal everything they saw attractive (ἀγώγιμον), so that for the praised the encomium might be completed, and for those remaining at once zeal (ζῆλος) toward virtue (ἀρετή) and exhortation (παράκλησις); but for the most part wove (ἐξυφαίνω) the speech with myths (μῦθοι) and endless fictions (πλάσματα), the hymned not having praise from their own home (οἴκοθεν); how shall we, covering (καλύπτω) the very true and venerable things, really existing for all as procurers (πρόξενα) of all blessing (εὐλογία) and salvation, the matter of speech, in depths (βυθοί) of silence, not owe (ὀφλισκάνω) much laughter (γέλως), and meet the same judgement (δίκη) as the one who hid (κατακρύπτω) the talent (τάλαντον)? taking thought for the brevity (συντομία) of the speech, so that it become not hostile (πολέμιος) to the hearing (ἀκοαί), like food excessive for bodies.
pass_b_english: You see, fathers and brothers dear to God, the grace of this present day. Do you see the height and majesty of her who is now being praised? Are not her mysteries awe-inspiring? Are they not full of wonder? Blessed are those who see, as it is most fitting to see; blessed are those who have gained the perception of the mind! What flashes of light make this present night bright! What escorts of angels make radiant the falling asleep of the Mother who is the source of life! What God-inspired words of the apostles bless the burial of the God-receiving body! How does the Word of God, who in his compassion was pleased to become her son, receive her holy soul, serving this all-holy and most divine woman with his sovereign hands as his mother?

O good Lawgiver! Though not subject to the law, he fulfils the law which he himself commanded. For it was he who laid down that children should render to their parents what is due: "Honour," he says, "your father and your mother" (Exodus 20:12). That this is true is plain, I think, to anyone who has been initiated even a little into the divine oracles of Holy Scripture. For if, as divine Scripture says, "the souls of the righteous are in the hand of the Lord" (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1), does she not much more commit her soul into the hands of her Son and God? The word is true, and beyond all dispute.

But, if you are willing, let us go through who she is, and where she came from, and how, granted to this present life, she was given as a gift loftier and dearer than all the gifts of God; and what manner of life she led in this world, and of what mysteries she was found worthy. For if the Greeks, honouring the departed with funeral orations, eagerly brought together everything they saw that might appeal, so that the praise might be complete for the one praised, and for those left behind might be at once a spur to virtue and an encouragement; and if, for the most part, they wove their speech out of myths and endless fictions, since those they praised had no praise of their own; how shall we not incur great ridicule, and meet the same judgement as the one who hid the talent (Matthew 25:25), if we hide in the depths of silence, as the saying goes, things utterly true and worthy of reverence, things that truly bring every blessing and salvation to all? And we shall take care to keep our speech short, so that it may not become an enemy to the ears, as too much food is to the body.

choices.note: Wisdom 3:1 has "in the hand of God";
John writes "of the Lord"; translated as John has it.
"Commit her soul into the hands" (παρατίθεται) may echo Luke 23:46; left uncited.
"Above all contradiction" may echo Hebrews 7:7 (χωρὶς πάσης ἀντιλογίας); left uncited.
"Not subject to the law, he fulfils the law" may echo Matthew 5:17 and Galatians 4:4; left uncited.
ζωαρχικός ("life-originating") rendered "the source of life".
οἷα μητρί rendered "as his mother"; the participle λειτουργῶν ("serving") is kept subordinate to ὑποδέχεται ("receives").
τὸ τοῦ λόγου is the idiom "as the saying goes" (applied to "the depths of silence").
ἀγώγιμον ("attractive, persuasive") rendered "that might appeal".
"The Greeks" (Ἕλληνες) means the pagan Greeks, whose funeral orations (epitaphioi) are meant.
The sentence about the Lady and her soul has no question mark in the edition but reads as a rhetorical question; so rendered.
The participial last clause ("taking thought for the brevity of the speech") is made a separate sentence.
μεταμεμυημένων is an odd form;
Reg. reads μεμυημένων; both mean "initiated".
Edition variants: (90) R.
φιλόθεοι for φίλοι Θεῷ (same sense);
"possible and most fitting";
(92) Germ.
ὑποδύεται for ὑποδέχεται; the printed "receives" is kept;
κατορύξαντι ("buried") for κατακρύψαντι ("hid"); the printed reading is confirmed on the page image and kept.
